<a id="Compiler.alias_expression"></a>
#### Compiler.alias_expression

`List Compiler.alias_expression(Compiler c)`

Returns the expression that the identifier at the cursor stands for when
it names a visible alias, or NULL. A declaration in a scope inside the
alias's scope shadows it. The expression keeps its bindings where a
later declaration hides one of their names.

Source: `src/macros/aliases.x:433`

<a id="Compiler.alias_form_starts"></a>
#### Compiler.alias_form_starts

`int Compiler.alias_form_starts(Compiler c)`

Reports whether the cursor begins an alias or its removal. An alias is
the word `alias`, or at file scope `static alias`, then an expression
followed by `as` or a braced body; a removal is `unalias name;`. Each
word stays an ordinary name where it continues an operand, as in
`alias = value;`, and where it names a type that no `as` follows. This
query does not consume tokens.

Source: `src/macros/aliases.x:67`

#### Compiler.lower_replacement

`List Compiler.lower_replacement(Compiler c, List replacement, List source)`

Lowers `replacement`, which `Compiler.rewrite_lowered` bound for the

Source: `src/macros/rewrites.x:265`

<a id="Compiler.lower_rewrite"></a>
#### Compiler.lower_rewrite

`List Compiler.lower_rewrite( Compiler c, Symbol point, Var kind, List source, Symbol position, Type expected, Token site)`

Binds and lowers a replacement while its rule remains active. The
source expressions the replacement holds lower outside the rule, so a
nested use of the rule applies again. A statement replacement, or a
lowered one, also lowers the statements its source held outside the
rule, and lowers once, so a new statement it writes stays outside the
rule. Code a shipped rule's replacement writes, such as the support call
an interpolated String or a collection literal lowers to, is not source,
so only shipped rules see it. An expression retains the result type
already established for its parent. A replacement whose template and
slot signatures an earlier use in the unit prepared lowers only its
captured values.

Source: `src/macros/rewrites.x:299`

<a id="Compiler.parse_alias_declaration"></a>
#### Compiler.parse_alias_declaration

`List Compiler.parse_alias_declaration(Compiler c, int skip_body)`

Parses an alias or its removal at file scope. A semicolon alias returns
NULL; its name stays visible to the rest of the unit and, unless it is
`static`, to the files that include this one. `unalias` also returns
NULL. A braced alias returns `(seq ...)` of the
top-level forms it wraps, which keep their file-scope placement while
the name ends at the closing brace. Collection, with `skip_body`, reads
the wrapped forms as it reads any other. Inside a template the name is
the template's own, as at block scope.

Source: `src/macros/aliases.x:169`

<a id="Compiler.parse_alias_member"></a>
#### Compiler.parse_alias_member

`List Compiler.parse_alias_member( Compiler c, Symbol position, List context)`

Parses an alias among the members of an aggregate or enum body, where
`position` is `<field>` or `<enumerator>` and `context` is the
aggregate type. Its name ends with the body. A braced alias returns
`(seq ...)` of the members it wraps; a semicolon alias and `unalias`
return `(seq)`.

Source: `src/macros/aliases.x:224`

<a id="Compiler.parse_alias_statement"></a>
#### Compiler.parse_alias_statement

`List Compiler.parse_alias_statement(Compiler c, int block)`

Parses an alias or its removal in a function body or a template. The
semicolon form and `unalias` change the current scope and return
`(seq)`; they require block position, which `block` reports. The braced
form returns its block, with the name defined in a scope around it.

Source: `src/macros/aliases.x:139`

#### Compiler.rebound

`void Compiler.rebound(Compiler c, Var source, List bound)`

Records that binding built the statement `bound` again from `source`,
a value the active lowering watches, so it watches `bound` as well. A
statement without an origin, such as an unbraced body, keeps nothing
else that identifies it when a binder it uses binds again.

#### Compiler.rebuild_expression

`List Compiler.rebuild_expression(Compiler c, Type type, List application)`

Rebuilds an expression from a pending Macro value application, preserving
its established root `type`, child stage, and source wrappers. Binding,
capture collection, hygiene, and effects do not run, and a statement
expression's template-origin wrappers are omitted.

<a id="Compiler.rewrite"></a>
#### Compiler.rewrite

`List Compiler.rewrite( Compiler c, Symbol point, Var kind, List source, Symbol position, Type expected, Token site)`

Matches registered patterns for one operation, then binds the first
replacement. A translator declines with void, null, or its input itself.
Active rules cannot re-enter. A statement of the same kind that a
statement replacement writes or copies, such as its source, takes the
rules after the one that replaced it.

Source: `src/macros/rewrites.x:246`

<a id="Compiler.rewrite_lowered"></a>
#### Compiler.rewrite_lowered

`List Compiler.rewrite_lowered( Compiler c, Symbol point, Var kind, List source, Symbol position, Type expected, Token site)`

Matches registered patterns for the statement `source`, which the
transform has lowered, then binds the first replacement as
`Compiler.rewrite` does. Binding keeps the source, and each part of it
the replacement holds, as lowered.

Source: `src/macros/rewrites.x:256`

<a id="Compiler.rewrite_written"></a>
#### Compiler.rewrite_written

`List Compiler.rewrite_written( Compiler c, Symbol kind, List source, Type expected)`

Binds the replacement a shipped rule gives the lowered statement
`source` of `kind`, which the kernel wrote while lowering, as
`Compiler.rewrite_lowered` does. A statement the kernel writes is not
source, so no program rule sees it.

<a id="Compiler.take_code_value"></a>
#### Compiler.take_code_value

`int Compiler.take_code_value( Compiler c, Var input, Var &value, int &retained)`

Consumes a `(code-value STAGE CODE EFFECTS)` carrier a producer returned
into a macro value application, or that `Compiler.bind_code_value`
binds as one. Effects are applied in order under the application's
transaction, and their tokens are replaced in the code.
`retained` reports a bound or lowered stage, which ordinary binding
leaves untouched. Lowered code is not searched for a leftover binder.
Returns 0 for any other value.

<a id="Compiler.try_parse_macro_slot"></a>

`List Compiler.try_parse_macro_slot(Compiler c, Symbol role)`

Parses a macro hole or meta call slot for `role` while reading a

<a id="Compiler.try_parse_macro_subpattern"></a>
#### Compiler.try_parse_macro_subpattern

`List Compiler.try_parse_macro_subpattern(Compiler c, int content)`

Parses `$NAME(P, ...)` in a pattern, where each argument is a pattern,
into the pattern for code NAME builds with each argument pattern in its
hole. It matches the shelled expression or its bare content; `content`

Parses a direct or keyword-alias macro at the requested syntax position.

<a id="Compiler.watched_step"></a>
#### Compiler.watched_step

`Ast Compiler.watched_step(Compiler c, Ast ast)`

Lowers `ast` when it is a value the active lowering watches; NULL
otherwise. A preparing watch also records what lowering produced. A
value that an enclosing replacement's source held as well lowers outside
that replacement's rule too, and that replacement still watches its own
values within it.

Source: `src/macros/rewrites.x:730`

## Design notes

This module owns macro expansion. Expansion fills a definition's
template from an invocation's captures and binds the result through the
operations that bind parsed source. A definition is a compiler-only
`macrodef` List: its holes, a Match pattern over an invocation's
capture rows, and a template of the binders that pattern captures.
A template's meta-call slots, `$name(...)` and `@name(...)`, run native
`meta` functions through the unit's `MetaBindings`.
